claims.text: Adding a low concentration of Al to an elemental Cr coating will form an Al-rich interlayer or oxide at the coating/Zr-alloy interface.
The Al-rich interfacial phase will act as a diffusion barrier that suppresses Cr–Zr interdiffusion during high-temperature steam exposure.
Al modification will preserve protective coating performance under normal subcritical-water conditions.
The intervention is alloying the Cr coating with a controlled low concentration of Al by DC magnetron sputtering.
The intervention produces a modified TiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy-alloy coating variant.
Approximately 350°C represents the normal subcritical-water operating condition relevant to the coating.
Steam exposure near 1200°C represents an accident-relevant condition for the coating.
The interfacial mediator may be a Cr–Al intermetallic phase or aluminum oxide.
Al preferentially oxidizes or forms intermetallic compounds at the Cr-coating/Zr-substrate interface.
The resulting interfacial phase is robust enough to limit atomistic mixing between Cr and Zr.
Limiting Cr–Zr intermixing will mitigate premature coating failure at high temperature.
Compared with elemental Cr, the Al-modified coating will exhibit significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion in high-temperature steam.
Reduced interdiffusion will improve coating integrity and longevity under both normal-operation and accident conditions.
The proposed barrier is expected to remain effective up to approximately 1200°C during transient steam exposure.
The proposed coating is expected to perform reliably at approximately 350°C.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis proposes an Al-alloyed Cr coating, but the intervention identifies the product as a TiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy. TiCrZrNbTa contains no stated Al and is materially distinct from a low-Al Cr coating.

The baseline and initial state describe elemental Cr on Zr alloy, whereas the intervention switches to a multicomponent TiCrZrNbTa coating without explaining whether Al is added to Cr, to TiCrZrNbTa, or whether the elemental-Cr architecture is retained.
The boundary refers to established exposure-time limits, but no numerical exposure duration is specified for either long-term water operation or transient steam exposure.
